title: Discovery: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment - Vara Pharma
summary: High-level discovery on on-prem, air-gapped deployment needs for regulated pharma. Key concerns: offline updates, hardware constraints (GPU types, NVMe), KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, SOC2/ISO equivalence, SSO/SAML, network isolation and installation process. Agreed to a POC scoping workshop and to share security docs and sizing.
topics: Hardware sizing (A100 vs H100, memory, NVMe)
next_steps: Alex to send SOC2 and security whitepaper by 2026-04-16
Priya to prepare initial hardware sizing and on-prem installation checklist by 2026-04-18
Schedule POC scoping call with Vara infra + security week of 2026-04-20
Provide preliminary pricing for Dedicated reserved capacity and Private deployment options
action_items: Alex Chen: Send SOC2 report, security whitepaper, and link to network checklist by 2026-04-16
Priya Rao: Draft hardware sizing options (A100/H100/RTX options) and estimated throughput for 1k qps by 2026-04-18
Marko Petrovic: Share existing server inventory, rack specs, and whether HSM/KMS is already on-prem by 2026-04-17
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-04-14 | Start: 14:30 PT | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Dr. Emily Santos (Vara Head of AI), Marko Petrovic (Vara IT), Sara Liu (Vara Compliance), Tom Weaver (Vara Procurement)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick introductions?
[00:06] Dr. Emily Santos: Hi, Emily here, head of AI at Vara. We're exploring options for running LLM inference in our on-prem environment, must be air-gapped.
[00:14] Alex Chen: Great, thanks. Priya is our SE, she'll cover technicals.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Hi all. Quick agenda — understand constraints, current infra, update process for models, and compliance requirements.
[00:27] Marko Petrovic: From infra, we have two datacenters, mostly Dell racks, current GPU inventory is mixed — some older A100s and a few newly purchased H100s on order.
[00:39] Sara Liu: Compliance: all patient and trial data must never leave our network. We require audit logs, key management via our HSM, and an air-gapped update workflow.
[00:49] Alex Chen: Understood. So the conversation is Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — I assume you're leaning Private/on-prem air-gapped?
[00:56] Dr. Emily Santos: Yes. We evaluated hosted, but regulators won't allow external inference for the clinical models.
[01:03] Priya Rao: Ok. Quick question on updates — do you have a process for offline signed artifacts? how do you want model updates delivered when the cluster is not internet-connected?
[01:12] Marko Petrovic: We currently do signed tarballs via secure courier for firmware. For models, we'd prefer signed model bundles we can verify locally using our HSM.
[01:21] Priya Rao: That aligns with Redwood Private — we can support offline update packages that are signed; SE note: will need a verification process integrated with customer KMS/HSM for signature verification and key rotation.
[01:33] Tom Weaver: Cost question — what's the delta between Dedicated reserved capacity in cloud vs full Private on-prem licensing?
[01:40] Alex Chen: We can provide both pricing tracks — Dedicated reserved is usage/commit in our infra; Private is a licensing + support + optional install bundle. We'll send detailed pricing, but expect on-prem to have an upfront platform fee plus optional installation support.
[01:53] Dr. Emily Santos: On hardware — how sensitive is Redwood to GPU differences? we worry about A100 vs H100 perf differences and also NVMe caching needs for kv cache.
[02:01] Priya Rao: Performance and kernel selection varies. H100s will give better throughput for some attention kernels, but A100s still work. For very large context, NVMe-backed KV cache and local persistent storage helps. We'll provide sizing guidance — ballpark is drive IOPS and memory per model.
[02:18] Marko Petrovic: Any constraints on network egress ports during install? we have strict firewall rules.
[02:23] Priya Rao: We can do an offline install. For air-gapped we provide a package; for the control plane we can either expose a minimal management plane in a DMZ or run fully customer-managed control plane.
[02:35] Sara Liu: We also need RBAC mapping to our SAML/Okta. And full audit logs retained for at least 5 years for regulatory audits.
[02:43] Alex Chen: Redwood Private supports SAML SSO and can forward audit logs to your ELK/Splunk. We'll include retention options.
[02:50] Dr. Emily Santos: How do you handle fallback models if a larger model can't run on some racks? we need graceful degradation not to break clinical tooling.
[02:58] Priya Rao: You can pin model versions and have routing policies — fallbacks to smaller quantized variants are supported. Also canary rollouts for model updates.
[03:07] Tom Weaver: For POC do you provide any hardware? or do we need to procure?
[03:11] Alex Chen: We typically recommend customer-provided hardware, but we can assist with partner referrals and install services. For air-gapped we do not ship hardware ourselves by default.
[03:20] Marko Petrovic: About key management — we have a Thales HSM. Can Redwood integrate with on-prem HSM and perform key wrapping?
[03:28] Priya Rao: Yes, Redwood supports KMS integrations and HSM-backed key storage for secrets. For air-gapped setup, we support locally stored keys and rotation via signed commands. We'll validate integration during POC.
[03:40] Dr. Emily Santos: Are there certifications or security docs you can share now?
[03:44] Alex Chen: We'll share SOC2 report, pen test summary, and our private deployment security whitepaper after the call.
[03:50] Marko Petrovic: Anything about model provenance and reproducibility? we need to know the exact model binary used for each inference for audit trails.
[03:57] Priya Rao: We can embed model hashes and maintain versioned artifacts — and our runtime supports logging model id per request for traceability.
[04:06] Tom Weaver: Timeline — we're targeting a pilot in June if the procurement cycle moves quickly. Decision by end of Q2 ideally.
[04:14] Alex Chen: Good. Next step: we'll send docs and schedule a POC scoping with your infra and security. Any final concerns?
[04:22] Sara Liu: Offline update chain-of-custody — we'll want a documented process and signatures.
[04:27] Priya Rao: We'll include an offline update playbook and example signed bundle flow.
[04:32] Dr. Emily Santos: Great, thanks. Looking forward to the sizing and pricing.
[04:36] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up.
[04:40] [crosstalk] End of recording.
